name: Physics: predicting newly measured nuclear masses from the AME2016 evaluation
description: Fit a nuclear mass model on the experimental masses of the 2016 Atomic Mass Evaluation and predict the mass excesses of the 71 nuclides first measured in time for AME2020. The candidate never sees the AME2020 values, and the score is the root-mean-square deviation from them in keV.

sources.locator: Moeller, Sierk, Ichikawa and Sagawa (2016), FRDM(2012): a global macroscopic-microscopic model whose purpose is predicting ground-state masses of known and unknown nuclei.
Duflo and Zuker (1995), Microscopic mass formulas: a compact global mass model fitted to measured masses and used to extrapolate.
Wang, Liu, Wu and Meng (2014), Surface diffuseness correction in global mass formula (WS4): a mass model built for accurate extrapolation.
AME2016 tables (Wang et al. 2017); experimental entries form the training data and the '#' estimates the context baseline. File: https://www-nds.iaea.org/amdc/ame2016/mass16.txt.
AME2020 tables (Wang et al. 2021, CC BY 3.0); the experimental entries absent from AME2016 are the held-out targets. File: https://www-nds.iaea.org/amdc/ame2020/mass_1.mas20.txt.

requirements.datasets: Derived from the pinned AME2016 and AME2020 AMDC files by python3 scripts/prepare_bio_physics.py (hashes in catalog/bio_physics-data-lock.json).

evaluation.benchmark: Physics: predicting newly measured nuclear masses from the AME2016 evaluation
evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

execution.interface: predict_masses(training, queries) -> list of len(queries) atomic mass excesses in keV. training is a list of dicts with keys N, Z, A, element, mass_excess_keV and uncertainty_keV: the 2408 experimental (non-estimated) entries of the Atomic Mass Evaluation 2016 with N, Z >= 8. queries is a list of [N, Z] pairs: the 71 nuclides with N, Z >= 8 that are experimental in AME2020 but were missing or only estimated in AME2016. predict_masses runs in a sandboxed subprocess that never sees the AME2020 values, with a 120 s CPU budget. Score (minimize): root-mean-square deviation in keV between the predictions and the AME2020 mass excesses; predictions outside [-200000, 300000] keV, NaN or a wrong length are invalid

limitations: The held-out set is small (71 nuclides) and defined by which masses happened to be measured between the two evaluations, so it is not a uniform sample of the unknown region and the RMS is noisy.

Both evaluations are public and so are their later successors, so a candidate tuned on this split can overfit it; any improvement should be checked on masses measured after AME2020 before a scientific claim.
Training uses the AME2016 values as published; some of them were revised in AME2020, and the AME2020 targets carry their own uncertainties, which the unweighted RMS ignores.
The AMDC files state no licence; they are downloaded by the prepare script and not redistributed.

state_of_the_art.statement: No published value for this exact split. For context, the AME2016 evaluators' own extrapolated estimates of 69 of the 71 targets deviate from the AME2020 measurements by 213 keV RMS (computed from the two published tables), and the liquid-drop seed gives 3121 keV.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Predict the masses of atomic nuclei that have not yet been measured.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Nuclear masses set reaction energies and drip lines and feed astrophysical r-process networks; global mass models are built and judged by how well they extrapolate to newly measured nuclides, and their residuals remain of order a few hundred keV.

papers.title: Nuclear ground-state masses and deformations: FRDM(2012)
papers.primary_goal: Build a global nuclear mass model that predicts ground-state masses, including for nuclei that have not been measured.
papers.task_relation: The task asks for exactly this kind of model and scores it on nuclides measured only after the training evaluation.

papers.title: Surface diffuseness correction in global mass formula
papers.primary_goal: Improve a global nuclear mass formula and its extrapolation accuracy.
papers.task_relation: Represents the class of models the task measures, judged by RMS deviation in keV.

science_relevance.reason: The cited papers' main research goal is predicting nuclear masses, and the evaluator scores exactly that on held-out measurements.
science_relevance.verification_basis: Crossref metadata inspected; the AME table parser was checked by recomputing the tabulated binding energy per nucleon of 56Fe, and the AME2016 evaluators' own extrapolations were scored with the task metric (213 keV RMS).
